findings: All three Skillsta funnels ask users to type a verification code right after the email. Of the competitors captured, only Copymind does this; Breeze, Simply Piano, MemoryOS and SmartyMe go straight from email to the plan and paywall.

Skillsta's weakest step is Loader → Email: 11% of users who reach the loader submit an email in Vocal funnel 2.0, against 24% in the Vocal Scanner, whose email screen says “Your results are ready… full voice analysis”.
Email → paywall holds at 97% in the Vocal Scanner but only 24% in Vocal funnel 2.0, although both show the same code screen, so something else after email submit is losing users in 2.0.

Of the 9 competitor paywalls captured, most show a discount (50–63% off at Simply Piano, MemoryOS, Chillio, Learna, SmartyMe, Simply Draw) and 6 run a countdown timer; Breeze, MemoryOS, Copymind and SmartyMe add a money-back guarantee.
Learna (Genesis, UK) is the most active launcher: 154 active ads, 50 started in the last two weeks. Imprint (580) and Simply Piano (430) run the most ads overall; Copymind has none running.
Paywalls not captured this run: Skillsta (email code), Imprint and Yousician (need an account), Simply Sing (walk stops at the voice question).
comparison_notes: Skillsta Vocal funnel 2.0 asks about 25 questions with 7 value or social-proof screens before the email gate. Simply Piano alternates almost 1:1 (12 questions, 11 value screens) and MemoryOS follows most answers with a reassurance screen (“No worries! We got you!”).
Skillsta and competitors reach the email gate at a similar depth (screen 33 vs 26–36), so length alone doesn't set Skillsta apart.
The Vocal Scanner and Breeze frame the email as unlocking a ready result (“Your results are ready”), while Vocal funnel 2.0 asks for an email “to get your personal plan”.
Skillsta's paywall isn't captured yet because it sits behind the email code; competitor paywall structure is in the table above.

hypotheses.title: Frame the Vocal 2.0 email gate as unlocking a ready result
hypotheses.seen_in: Skillsta Vocal Scanner (24% loader → email), Breeze “Your results are ready · Explore results”
hypotheses.change: Replace “Enter your email to get your personal plan” with a results-ready screen that names what they'll get (vocal range, strengths, voice match) and a blurred preview
hypotheses.impact: Estimate: could move toward the Scanner's 24%

hypotheses.title: Find and fix the post-email loss in Vocal 2.0
hypotheses.seen_in: Same code screen in Scanner (97% email → paywall) vs Vocal 2.0 (24%)
hypotheses.change: Compare what happens after email_submit in both funnels (screens, redirects, event firing); if it's the code step, test showing the plan and paywall before verification as Breeze, Simply Piano and MemoryOS do
hypotheses.impact: Estimate: largest single lever if the gap is a real drop and not a tracking difference

hypotheses.title: Add a reassurance screen after key answers
hypotheses.seen_in: MemoryOS (question → “Weak memory is not your fault”), Simply Piano (12 questions, 11 value screens)
hypotheses.change: Insert 3–4 short value screens that reply to the user's previous answer, and cut low-value questions to keep length flat
hypotheses.impact: Estimate: a few points of quiz completion

hypotheses.title: Test a timed discount plus money-back guarantee on the paywall
hypotheses.seen_in: SmartyMe (60% off, 10-min timer, 28-day money-back), MemoryOS (63% off, timer), Learna (60% off, 10-min timer), Simply Piano (50% off, 15-min timer)
hypotheses.change: Check the current paywall against these; add the missing pieces one at a time
hypotheses.impact: Estimate: small lift on purchase rate

hypotheses.title: Show per-day prices and a live “people chose” ticker
hypotheses.change: Add per-day price under each plan and a recent-choices strip above the plans
